**Merge keeps the history, rebase rewrites it.**

A merge ties the two branches together with a new commit. Everything that happened stays as it happened.

A rebase lifts your commits off and replays them on the new base. You get a straight line, but every commit gets a new ID.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph merge
    A1[main] --> M((merge commit))
    B1[your branch] --> M
  end
  subgraph rebase
    A2[main] --> C1[your commits, replayed on top]
  end
```

Reach for rebase on your own branch, before anyone else has it. Reach for merge when the branch is shared with others.

The one rule: never rebase commits someone else has already pulled. Their copy and yours stop matching, and the cleanup hurts.
